co_happy_hour_crag.blurb: A roadside wall in Boulder Canyon, west of Boulder, that suits an evening session or an easy weekend day. Most of the 29 climbs are single-pitch trad lines, with a few top-rope setups and a couple of bolted routes. Grades start around 5.5 and run to the low 5.12s, but the heart of the crag is 5.7 to 5.9, where the grippy granite rewards steady footwork. The wall looks south, so it soaks up sun for much of the day and feels pleasant in cool weather. Heights are modest, roughly 70 to 120 feet. The short, steep hike up is a good fit for newer trad leaders, and the best lines tend to sit toward the middle of the face.

co_mill_creek_crag.blurb: A compact outcrop above Mill Creek near Dumont, west of Denver, at roughly 9,500 feet. Of its 29 climbs, most are bolted sport lines, with a smaller group of trad routes and one top-rope option. Grades are spread widely, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.11 range and a handful of harder lines above that, including a single 5.13. The wall faces south, so it warms up quickly on sunny days, which makes it a useful choice outside summer. Once quiet, it now draws a steady crowd, and several parties at a time is common on weekends. The walk to the base is very short, and a longer scramble leads to the top for anchors.

co_hallett_peak.blurb: A big alpine wall of roughly 1,000 feet above Emerald Lake in Rocky Mountain National Park, near Estes Park, reached from the Bear Lake side. The climbing is mostly long multi-pitch alpine routes, with a few shorter trad lines. Summer rock grades run from around 5.7 up to a single 5.13, centered on 5.8 to 5.10, and winter brings snow, ice and mixed objectives. The face splits into three buttresses divided by chimneys: the middle one is the busiest, while the far one is quieter. The wall points toward the northeast, so it stays cool in warm weather, and protection can be sparse. Expect a committed day with exposure, so previous alpine and trad experience matters.

co_lower_bridge_to_scottish_gullies.blurb: The downstream stretch of the Ouray Ice Park, in the Uncompahgre Gorge by the town of Ouray, covering the walls under the lower bridge as far as the Scottish gully. This is an ice and mixed zone, with water supplied by the park's pipes. Ice grades cluster around WI4 and WI5, with a few easier pitches, and the mixed lines run from about M7 to M10. The gorge opens to the sun on clear days, so ice can thin, and this stretch fills up on winter weekends. Anchors and lines can be hard to spot in a crowd, and several of the east-side climbs are reached by rappel from above. Good for strong ice climbers wanting variety.

co_long_s_peak_mt_meeker_cirque.blurb: The high cirque between Longs Peak and Mt. Meeker in Rocky Mountain National Park, a serious alpine setting mostly visited for ice and mixed climbing. The 29 climbs here are largely ice, from easy water ice up to hard WI5 and WI6 routes, plus several mixed lines in the lower M grades and a few snowy or rocky alpine routes. Ice forms over much of the year in a good season, but the drips are short-lived and conditions change fast, so making the full walk toward Chasm Lake is the best way to judge them. Distances look short but the approach is long, and descents and weather deserve respect.

co_north_face_3.blurb: The main face of Crystal Wall in Poudre Canyon, west of Fort Collins, across the highway from the river. It has 29 routes, mostly bolted lines that are set up for top-roping, plus a few lead sport routes. Grades run from the 5.8 range up to a couple of 5.13s, with most of the climbing at 5.11 and 5.12, so it leans toward intermediate and strong climbers. The wall faces north and sits in shade. Some routes have two pitches, and the character is scenic and fairly adventurous, with a view across to the neighboring cliffs. The walk to the base is short but steep and rough.
co_north_face_3.parking_note: Pull off at one of the roadside spots on Highway 14 just beyond the tunnel west of Mishawaka, then cross over to the foot of the rocks.

co_bbc_boulder.blurb: A large boulder in the Satellite Boulders, a short hike above Chautauqua Park in the Flatirons of Boulder. Its 29 problems lie around several sides of the rock and cover a wide range: easy V0 and V1 problems, a middle group from V2 to V5, and a cluster of hard V6 to V9 testpieces. It is one of the busiest spots among the Satellites, so expect other climbers and plan to share pads and space. A smaller warm-up boulder with easy problems sits nearby.

co_wicked_cave_the.blurb: A steep wall beside a large roofed bowl in Rifle Mountain Park, a limestone canyon near Rifle. All 29 routes are bolted sport climbs, and they are hard: the grades start around 5.11 and are mostly 5.13 and 5.14, with one a notch higher. Expect sustained endurance climbing that stays demanding right to the anchors, on steep rock with varied features. The lower section of the wall is a little scaly and can be damp, while the upper stone is solid. Summers can feel muggy and buggy here because of the lack of breeze, so fall tends to be more pleasant. This is a destination for experienced sport climbers.
